text: There is an AI mega-trend happening in China that the West is largely ignoring: AI-generated content Long-form video. Entire AI-generated dramas. AI music. Advertising. Animation And it's scaling FAST Some numbers: - In the first 8 months of 2026, China produced 13x as many short/mini dramas as ALL of 2025 - AI video generation is now faster than human consumption speed. A 5-second video can be generated in ~3 seconds - On Aug. 31, Hunan TV/Mango TV aired “Beyond Wukong,” the first AI-generated long-form production to hit Chinese satellite primetime. 30 episodes × 40 minutes. The first 5 episodes alone generated 300M views on Mango TV, with production costs reportedly ~90% below comparable live-action/CG productions - The Global AI music industry hit $6.65B in 2025, +28% YoY. China's market exceeded ¥10B. Suno disclosed >2M paying users and ~$300M ARR in March 2026 - One AI-generated song, “Death of Monkey King,” pulled 17.1M views on Bilibili - Across animation, music, TVCs and short dramas, AI is estimated to cut production costs 80–95% and turnaround times by 5–10x Sounds like a massive new consumer revolution, right? But then I looked at WHO is consuming it in China.. And here's the twist: It's not primarily China's youth. The Chinese youth are memeing about "AI slop" just like we are in the West, “数字泔水” (Digital Slop), “AI味儿” (AI Smell).. So who's watching all the AI generated content in China? - 57.5% of AI-generated-content consumers are over 30 - The largest cohort is 45+, accounting for an estimated 49.4% of AI short-drama viewers In other words, China's AI-content boom may look radically different from what we're imagining The West often talks about AI-generated content as “slop” and you don't have to look too deep to find that young people in the West view AI-generated content negatively. But China's older consumers appear to be embracing it And there's an interesting parallel here.. It only takes 30 seconds of scrolling through Facebook to see that American Boomers are already getting absolutely flooded with AI-generated images, videos and engagement bait and they're eating it up China may simply be further along the same curve: short-form content + algorithmic dopamine + AI-generated supply = an exponentially larger content firehose. They are staring straight into the Basilisk's eyes Sounds dystopian af, but there's a business lesson here: I've said it in previous posts that some of the most successful young people I've met over the last few years outside of high-paying W2 careers, nepotism, or VC fundraising are the ones that have figured out how to use modern technology to sell goods and services to Boomers Seems like AI content is following the same path for now. Or maybe AI-generated content gets so good that it eventually breaks through the “AI slop” stigma and captures younger audiences too Either way, I think this is a trend worth watching extremely closely as China may be giving us an early look at what happens when the marginal cost of content approaches zero

La volatilidad se ha reiniciado bruscamente en las últimas sesiones y se acerca a sus niveles mínimos naturales.

JPM situó la actividad minorista cerca del segundo percentil de su historia. El flujo semanal fue de 2.500 millones de dólares, frente a un promedio de 6.800 millones de dólares en los últimos doce meses, mientras que el sector tecnológico registró el tercer mayor volumen de reembolsos de fondos en el conjunto de datos. Sin embargo, Nvidia absorbió casi 1.200 millones de dólares de los 1.600 millones que llegaron a los Siete Magníficos. Fuera de las grandes empresas, el sector minorista vendió alrededor de 405 millones de dólares en acciones tecnológicas, 555 millones en acciones industriales y 493 millones en acciones de servicios de comunicación. Los bienes de consumo básico fueron el único sector con un flujo de acciones individual positivo. Las empresas más grandes dominan la ponderación de los índices, por lo que los principales índices pueden mantenerse firmes mientras que la acción promedio se debilita.

Los semiconductores han subido alrededor de un 51% este año, frente a aproximadamente un 10% del S&P 500 equiponderado y un 8% del ETF de las Magnificent Seven. ¿Momento de rotación?

La rotación también ha alcanzado a los fondos de dividendos, las utilities y el consumo básico. Estas exposiciones pueden comportarse como sustitutos de los bonos, porque sus dividendos compiten con las rentabilidades de la deuda pública. Las utilities ya se han debilitado a medida que la rentabilidad del Treasury a 10 años se acercaba al 5%, aunque las acciones diversificadas de dividendos se han mantenido más fuertes.
